research_rationale:
EO 13238 (signed 2001-12-05; 66 FR 63903, Federal Register of 2001-12-10, FR Doc. 01-30624) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13238.txt. It closes executive departments and agencies and excuses employees from duty on one named day (Monday, December 24, 2001), lets agency heads keep offices open for stated reasons, and treats that day as within the scope of EO 11582 and 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) for pay and leave. Every command is tied to that single day, so each clause ends by its own terms on 2001-12-24 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading would end the commands when that day began). A by-number search of the held order texts finds no later order citing this order, and the three machine searches record no later amendment, revocation or supersession. The one machine hit for this order in the Office of the Federal Register catalog search names EO 11582, which this order cites in its own text as signed February 11, 1971; an order signed in 1971 cannot be a later instrument, so it is not an end or amendment of this order. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

savings.reason: Employees excused from duty on the named day were excused under the order, and pay and leave for that day are governed by EO 11582 and the cited statutes, which the order only applied to the day; those accrued pay and leave effects rest on the cited authorities and do not keep the order operative after 2001-12-24. No held source shows any pending matter, exception or savings clause in the order.
